title: Brief to editable campaign
qualification: Actual application · bundled fictional brand · offline deterministic generation; live AI generation is not connected.

steps.title: Open a sample campaign
steps.text: Here is CampaignForge running locally. I will open its bundled fictional brand, so we can walk through the real application without client data or an API key.
steps.detail: The sample button executes the application's existing deterministic planner. This demonstrates the offline workflow, not a live AI model.

steps.title: Inspect the concepts
steps.text: The sample brief produces four different layouts. Each concept has a review score. I can compare the designs, then open one in the visual editor.
steps.detail: Concept scores are internal design checks, not measured sales performance. The four concepts are real editable documents.

steps.title: Edit the headline
steps.text: Now I select the headline layer and change the wording. The canvas updates immediately. This is editable text inside the product, not a flattened presentation image.
steps.detail: The recording changes a fictional campaign headline to GRAND OPENING. Only a fresh browser's local sample database is modified.

steps.title: Check the design
steps.text: Next I run the built-in review. It surfaces issues to check before delivery. These warnings stay visible because a working review system should show what still needs attention.
steps.detail: The product's review findings remain unaltered. This is local browser acceptance; packaged desktop and paid-release gates remain open.

steps.title: Export the result
steps.text: Finally I export a PNG from the edited document. The download is generated by the application. That is the workflow: a brief, editable concepts, human changes, review, and an output file.
steps.detail: The generated PNG is checked for a valid signature and saved as recording evidence. No provider or payment endpoint is called.

title: Explore the company and release roadmap
qualification: Actual local build of the company website · public information · no inquiry submitted.

steps.title: Start at headquarters
steps.text: This is the actual M3MM company website. The front page gives visitors a clear route into released work, website services, and the product roadmap.
steps.detail: Recorded from the existing local static build. Reachability, testing status and official release remain separate.

steps.title: Open the roadmap
steps.text: I open the roadmap to see the release queue. It distinguishes the official hub from testing previews and future plans, so investors can inspect the stage of each project.
steps.detail: Dates displayed inside the captured product are roadmap targets. This recording does not certify that a target was met.

steps.title: Filter testing previews
steps.text: Now I select the testing filter. The list narrows to preview builds instead of treating every repository as a launched product. This is the website's real filtering behavior.
steps.detail: The filter is clicked and its pressed state is asserted during recording. No product status is changed.

title: Explore the custom website sales flow
qualification: Actual local company services page · no contact form, email or payment submitted.

steps.title: See the service offer
steps.text: This is M3MM's custom website services page. I will walk through how a business evaluates the work and chooses a next step.
steps.detail: M3MM Websites is the custom delivery lane. It is separate from SiteGuide's do-it-yourself templates.

steps.title: Inspect client proof
steps.text: The proof section shows examples of delivered website work. It gives the prospect something concrete to inspect before discussing a project.
steps.detail: Client work demonstrates delivery capability. This recording does not establish conversion rates, current revenue or customer counts.

steps.title: Review the service ladder
steps.text: Next I move to the service options. A prospect can compare the scope and starting prices before asking for a review. I stop before sending any inquiry.
steps.detail: Prices on the recorded product are its existing public offer, not investor funding terms. No purchase or submission happens in this demo.

title: Browse and open a website template
qualification: Actual storefront and template files · preview navigation only · checkout and AI widget are not demonstrated.

steps.title: Browse the storefront
steps.text: This is SiteGuide's actual template storefront. It presents the template and widget offers, then lets a buyer preview the designs before deciding what fits.
steps.detail: The local capture uses public template files. Checkout, paid downloads and provider-backed widget responses are outside this recording.

steps.title: Choose a design
steps.text: I move to the template gallery and choose the wellness studio design. These are real preview links, so the next screen opens the template itself.
steps.detail: Soma is a bundled template example, not a claim that M3MM has a paying wellness-studio customer.

steps.title: Explore the preview
steps.text: Here is the selected template. I can scroll through its layout and content as a prospective buyer would. The design can be inspected without completing a purchase.
steps.detail: This proves storefront-to-preview navigation. External images and services are blocked in the isolated capture; it does not verify checkout or AI answering.

title: Try a lesson and see the feedback
qualification: Actual local learning app · fresh sample learner · written exercise only; no synthetic Vietnamese lesson audio.

steps.title: Inspect a fresh learner dashboard
steps.text: Southern Vietnamese Adaptive starts with a fresh learner profile. The dashboard has no invented progress. It asks for a baseline before adapting the practice.
steps.detail: The demo uses a new browser database. No personal progress or voice recordings are opened.

steps.title: Start the baseline
steps.text: I start the baseline assessment. The first written exercise explains why it was selected and asks the learner to identify a tone.
steps.detail: This is a working written exercise. Listening drills remain blocked until rights-cleared native-speaker recordings exist.

steps.title: Answer and inspect feedback
steps.text: I select an answer. The application checks it and gives immediate feedback. Then I move to the next question, showing the actual practice flow rather than a slide about it.
steps.detail: The click and resulting feedback are verified during capture. This short recording does not claim that a full learning outcome has been established.

title: Explore a 3D outdoor-living concept
qualification: Actual V2 preview · AI and 3D design concepts, not completed construction · client release review remains open.

steps.title: Open the concept preview
steps.text: This is the Aries Outdoor Living rebuild. It is a client preview, and the page labels its generated imagery as inspiration rather than completed construction photography.
steps.detail: This is the existing local V2 build. Client approval and the production swap remain separate gates; V1 is untouched.

steps.title: Start the 3D walkthrough
steps.text: I start the interactive three dimensional walkthrough. The visitor can explore a proposed outdoor space before discussing a build. This is a working scene inside the website.
steps.detail: The recorded browser runs the existing WebGL scene. It is a design concept, not a survey, engineering drawing or completed Aries project.

steps.title: Move onto the deck
steps.text: Now I choose the deck viewpoint. The camera moves through the scene, making the layout easier to understand. This kind of interaction gives a customer something useful to discuss.
steps.detail: The viewpoint button drives the existing scene camera. The recording does not substantiate construction quantities, costs or client conversion.

title: Inspect a branded audit report
qualification: Existing product sample report · fictional agency and fixture findings · no new audit run or customer result claimed.

steps.title: Open the report
steps.text: Teardown produces a self-contained branded audit report. This is the product's existing sample file, using a fictional agency. The scores and date belong to that sample, not a new scan.
steps.detail: Read-only copy of Teardown/docs/sample-report.html from the ThinkPad on October 10. It is a sample artifact, not current evidence about example.com or a customer.

steps.title: Inspect the priorities
steps.text: The report starts with an overall grade and the highest-priority findings. The format gives an agency a concrete starting point for a client conversation.
steps.detail: The sample's conversion language and scores are diagnostic output, not measured revenue loss or a guaranteed commercial outcome.

steps.title: Read the recommended fixes
steps.text: Scrolling down reveals the ranked fix list and practical next actions. This walkthrough shows the real report artifact. A separate end-to-end recording of the command-line audit is still needed.
steps.detail: No audit CLI is run in this recording. No customer website is scanned and no report is sent to anyone.

title: Explore the construction website’s two buyer paths
qualification: Actual local website prototype · placeholder contact details and claims remain unverified · no inquiry sent; release still awaits approved photography.

steps.title: Choose a project lane
steps.text: This is the actual Big Seven website prototype. The homepage separates commercial projects from residential work. This recording demonstrates navigation; the placeholder details and business claims are not verified.
steps.detail: Local source capture, not proof of client acceptance or production readiness. Existing photography and release gates remain.

steps.title: Explore commercial services
steps.text: I choose the commercial path. It opens a dedicated page for that audience, so visitors can examine the services before preparing an inquiry.
steps.detail: The click opens the real local commercial page. External requests and submissions are blocked.

steps.title: Switch to residential
steps.text: Now I switch to the residential path. The site gives homeowners a different service overview while keeping the same company navigation. I stop before contacting the business.
steps.detail: No email, form submission, quote or booking occurs.

title: Prepare a code-review request
qualification: Actual local intake interface · fictional sample request · no submission or delivery demonstrated.

steps.title: Understand the review offer
steps.text: Code Review Hub is the actual intake site for technical review requests. The page explains the offer before asking the visitor what they have built.
steps.detail: This demonstrates the current static candidate, not a deployed or accepted service.

steps.title: Enter a sample project
steps.text: I move into the request form and enter a fictional owner and sample project. The inputs are real controls. This does not use a customer record.
steps.detail: The browser starts clean. The email uses the reserved example domain; no real recipient is contacted.

steps.title: Describe the review need
steps.text: Next I describe the navigation and accessibility review in the message field. I stop before sending. This shows how a prospect prepares a request, not proof that the backend delivered it.
steps.detail: POST requests are blocked throughout capture. No successful-delivery response is fabricated.

title: Create and find a task on a fresh board
qualification: Actual local board · empty browser storage and fictional task · no existing work log or personal board data.

steps.title: Start with an empty board
steps.text: Cockpit opens in a fresh browser with an empty board. This is the actual local application, without private tasks or existing work logs.
steps.detail: An isolated browser storage fixture contains empty board and work-log arrays.

steps.title: Create a sample task
steps.text: I create a fictional website review task and give it a concrete next action. Saving places that task on the real board.
steps.detail: The task exists only in the disposable browser profile. It does not alter Michael’s normal board.

steps.title: Find the task
steps.text: I search for the sample website task. The board filters the visible cards, showing how a small team can find the next piece of work without an account or a server.
steps.detail: This is local browser behavior, not CockpitCloud collaboration or synchronization.

title: Explore a freshly generated owner guide
qualification: Actual HandoffKit output from its fictional bakery fixture · HTML guide generated locally · no screenshots, PDF or email delivery claimed.

steps.title: Open the generated guide
steps.text: This is a real owner guide generated by Handoff Kit from the bundled fictional bakery project. The command inspected that sample site and produced this HTML guide. It is not a real customer handoff.
steps.detail: Generated October 10 from examples/demo-site and demo.client.json with screenshots and PDF disabled. The source fixture has no photo folder.

steps.title: Find an editing task
steps.text: I select Manage your specials. The guide jumps to the instructions for the sample site’s detected content collection. The owner gets a concrete editing task rather than a general description of the tool.
steps.detail: This demonstrates navigation through generated output, not a recording of the generation command or a live edit to a customer site.

steps.title: Review support responsibilities
steps.text: Finally, I open ongoing support. The generated guide explains the sample support arrangement. These are fictional fixture terms, not a customer contract or the investor funding offer.
steps.detail: Only the HTML guide is shown. No support agreement, email or approval is sent.
